D. Program Plan
Two main lines of activity have been followed in Operation BREAKTHROUGH. The technical program is directed to encouraging the development of innovative building systems, evaluating these systems against performance—oriented criteria, developing prototype sites where these systems can be demonstrated free from restrictive constraints, and approving for volume production those systems which successfully complete the demonstration, testing and evaluation program.
At the same time, the market aggregation and development program is directed to endouraging state and local participation in the identification, development and aggregation of markets for housing; to working with states and localities to change the pattern of codes and regulations as they affect manufactured or industrialized housing; to encouraging more responsive labor and trade practices which will assist in the expansion of this part of the industry; and to working with the financial community to develop acceptance of industrialized housing as an appropriate investment.
i. The Technical Program
The technical program involved five separate, major national competitions:
 For innovative and production-oriented housing systems, specifically seeking those systems which were nearly ready for production, but which did require some additional development effort;
 For demonstration sites where these systems could be constructed without arbitrary restrictions for full and fair evaluation, and where new and innovative land use patterns could be tested and demonstrated;
 For site planning teams of architects, engineers, planners and landscape architects to develop and design innovative site plans providing better living at greater densities;
 For developer-manager who could assume the detailed day-to-day responsibility of site development, construction, management and marketing; and
 For a quality assurance consultant with the ability to provide technical expertise and inspection capability to insure that the housing, as produced, conforms to the designs as approved by HUD and the National Bureau of Standards.
